subject: maths
title: Angles and Lines: Turns, Right Angles, Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
seo_title: Year 3 Angles Worksheets: Turns, Right Angles, Horizontal, Vertical, Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
standard_text: Recognise angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn; identify right angles, recognise that two right angles make a half-turn, three make three quarters of a turn and four a complete turn; identify whether angles are greater than or less than a right angle; identify horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on angles and lines: quarter, half, three-quarter and whole turns, clockwise and anticlockwise, right angles in shapes, angles greater or less than a right angle, and horizontal, vertical, parallel and perpendicular lines. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: A right angle is a quarter turn: a square corner. Two make a half turn, three a three-quarter turn and four a whole turn.
key_sub: Compare every angle with a right angle: narrower is less, wider is greater. Arm length does not change an angle. Parallel lines never meet; perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.
body_html:
Angles are turns

An angle shows a turn. A quarter turn is a right angle. Clock hands turn clockwise. The other way is anticlockwise.

TurnRight angles
Quarter turn1
Half turn2
Three-quarter turn3
Whole turn4 (back to the start)
Example

Amelia faces north. She makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face now?

Clockwise goes north, east, south, west. One quarter turn from north is east.

Answer: east

Right angles

A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a page. It is 90°. A small square in a corner shows a right angle.

Make a right-angle checker: fold a piece of paper in half, then in half again.

Greater or less than a right angle

Put your checker in the angle. If the angle is narrower, it is less than a right angle (acute). If it is wider, it is greater than a right angle (obtuse).

Lines

Horizontal lines go straight across, like the horizon. Vertical lines go straight up and down. Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.

Example

How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?

The top and bottom are parallel. The left and right sides are parallel.

Answer: 2 pairs

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking longer arms make a bigger angleLook at how wide the angle opens
Mixing up horizontal and verticalHorizontal is like the horizon: straight across
Mixing up clockwise and anticlockwiseClockwise is the way clock hands go
Saying lines are parallel because they do not touch yetParallel lines stay the same distance apart
Saying a turned shape has no right anglesTurning a shape does not change its angles

faq.q: What do Year 3 children learn about angles?
faq.a: They learn that an angle is a turn, find right angles in shapes, and say whether an angle is greater or less than a right angle. Two right angles make a half turn and four make a whole turn.

faq.q: How do you explain a right angle to a Year 3 child?
faq.a: A right angle is a square corner, like the corner of a book. Fold a piece of paper in half and in half again to make a right-angle checker.

faq.q: What is the difference between parallel and perpendicular lines?
faq.a: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, like railway tracks. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle, like the corner of a page.

faq.q: Do Year 3 children need to know acute and obtuse angles?
faq.a: In Year 3 they say whether an angle is less than or greater than a right angle. The names acute and obtuse are part of the Year 4 curriculum, but many teachers start using them now.

sets.title: Quarter, half, three-quarter and whole turns

items.q: Which turn takes you back to where you started?
items.e: A whole turn goes all the way round (4 right angles), so you face the same way again.
The arrow goes three quarters of the way round, the opposite way to clock hands. That is anticlockwise.

items.q: Leo faces the door. He makes a half turn. What does he face now?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. The board is opposite the door.

items.q: Arjun faces the window. He makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. What does he face now?
items.e: Anticlockwise is the opposite way to clock hands. A quarter turn anticlockwise from the window is the door.
The arrow goes all the way round, back to the dashed line. That is a whole turn: 4 right angles.
The arrow goes three quarters of the way round, the same way as clock hands. That is clockwise.

items.q: How many right angles make a three-quarter turn?
items.e: A three-quarter turn is 3 right angles: three quarter turns.

items.q: Jack faces south. He makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: A quarter turn clockwise goes from south to west. Clockwise goes N, E, S, W.

items.q: How many right angles make a whole turn?
items.e: A whole turn is 4 right angles: four quarter turns take you all the way round.

items.q: How many right angles make a quarter turn?
items.e: A quarter turn is 1 right angle.

items.q: Kai faces east. He makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Count the quarter turns clockwise: east, south, west, north. Clockwise goes N, E, S, W.
The arrow goes three quarters of the way round. That is a three-quarter turn: 3 right angles.

items.q: How many right angles make a half turn?
items.e: A half turn is 2 right angles: 1 right angle + 1 right angle.

items.q: Harry faces north. He makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: A quarter turn clockwise goes from north to east. Clockwise goes N, E, S, W.

items.q: Ruby faces north. She makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does she face now?
items.e: A quarter turn anticlockwise goes from north to west. Anticlockwise goes N, W, S, E.

items.q: Which turn does the arrow show? It starts at the dashed line.
items.e: The arrow goes a quarter of the way round, the opposite way to clock hands. That is anticlockwise.

items.q: Which turn does the arrow show? It starts at the dashed line.
items.e: The arrow goes a quarter of the way round, the same way as clock hands. That is clockwise.

items.q: Which way do the hands on a clock turn?
items.e: Clock hands always turn the same way: clockwise. Anticlockwise is the opposite way.
The arrow goes halfway round, so the end line points the opposite way. That is a half turn: 2 right angles.

items.q: What turn does the arrow show? It starts at the dashed line.
items.e: The arrow goes a quarter of the way round. That is a quarter turn: 1 right angle.

sets.title: Right angles in shapes and around us

items.q: Which shape has exactly 1 right angle?
items.e: Picture B is a triangle with one square corner. The rectangle has 4, the other triangle has none and the 4-sided shape has 2.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The shape leans over. 2 corners are smaller and 2 are bigger than a right angle, so there are no right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: Only the bottom-left corner is a square corner. The other 2 corners are smaller.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The 2 bottom corners and the top of the roof are right angles. The 2 corners where the roof meets the walls are bigger.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: 6 corners are square corners. The 2 corners that point inwards are bigger than a right angle.

items.q: Which of these usually has 4 right angles?
items.e: A door is a rectangle, so it has 4 square corners. A pizza slice and a road sign have pointed corners.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: The 2 corners on the left are right angles. The 2 corners on the right are not.

items.q: How many right angles are inside the capital letter L?
items.e: Where the 2 lines of L meet, the inside corner is 1 right angle.

items.q: Which shape has no right angles?
items.e: Picture D leans over, so none of its corners are square corners. The turned square, the triangle and the L-shape all have right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: A square has 4 right angles. It is turned, but turning does not change the angles.

items.q: What does the small square in the corner show?
items.e: A small square in a corner shows a right angle: a square corner, like the corner of a page.

items.q: George says this shape has no right angles because it is turned. Is he right?
c: No, it still has 4 right angles
Yes, turned shapes have no corners
Yes, it has no right angles
items.e: It is a rectangle that has been turned. Turning a shape does not change its angles, so it still has 4 right angles.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: 5 corners are square corners. The corner that points inwards is bigger than a right angle, so do not count it.

items.q: Isla folds a piece of paper in half, then in half again. What does the folded corner make?
c: an angle greater than a right angle
items.e: Folding once makes a straight edge. Folding that edge in half again makes a right angle. This is a right-angle checker.

items.q: Which angle is a right angle?
items.e: Picture A makes a square corner. Its arms are short, but arm length does not change an angle.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: This shape has 6 corners, but they are all bigger than a right angle. So there are no right angles.

items.q: How many right angles are inside the capital letter T?
items.e: Where the top line meets the stem, there is a right angle on each side. That is 2 right angles.

items.q: Which angle is a right angle?
items.e: Picture C makes a square corner. It is turned, but it is still a right angle. Check with the corner of a piece of paper.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: 3 corners are still square corners. Cutting off a corner makes 2 corners that are bigger than a right angle.

items.q: How many right angles does this shape have?
items.e: All 3 corners are smaller than a right angle, so there are no right angles.

sets.title: Greater or less than a right angle

items.q: Which angle in this triangle is greater than a right angle?
items.e: Angle B, at the top, opens wider than a square corner. Angles A and C are narrow: less than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The angle opens wider than a square corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is less than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The angle opens wider than a square corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is less than a right angle.

items.q: Which angle is greater?
items.e: Angle Q opens wider than a right angle, and angle P is less than a right angle. So Q is greater, even though P has longer arms.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is less than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The angle opens wider than a square corner, so it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Grace says this angle is less than a right angle because its arms are short. Is she right?
c: No, it is greater than a right angle
No, it is a right angle
Yes, short arms make a small angle
Yes, it is a small turn
items.e: The size of an angle is how wide it opens, not how long its arms are. This angle opens wider than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The arms make a square corner, so it is a right angle. Turning an angle does not change it.

items.q: Which angle is greater than a right angle?
items.e: Picture B opens wider than a square corner. Its arms are short, but that does not make it small.

items.q: Ava says this angle is greater than a right angle because its arms are long. Is she right?
c: Yes, long arms make a big angle
No, it is a right angle
Yes, it is a straight line
No, it is less than a right angle
items.e: Long arms do not make an angle bigger. This angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is less than a right angle.

items.q: An angle that is greater than a right angle (but less than a straight line) has a special name. What is it?
items.e: An angle greater than a right angle but less than a straight line is called obtuse.

items.q: Which angle is less than a right angle?
items.e: Picture D is narrower than a square corner. The others are a right angle or wider.

items.q: Alfie puts his right-angle checker into an angle. The angle is wider than the checker. What is the angle?
items.e: The checker is a right angle. If the angle is wider than the checker, it is greater than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The angle is narrower than a square corner, so it is less than a right angle.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The arms make a square corner, so it is a right angle. Turning an angle does not change it.

items.q: Is this angle less than a right angle, a right angle or greater than a right angle?
items.e: The arms point in opposite directions and make a straight line: 2 right angles (a half turn).

items.q: An angle that is less than a right angle has a special name. What is it?
items.e: An angle less than a right angle is called acute. You will use this word a lot in Year 4.

items.q: A straight line is the same as how many right angles?
items.e: A straight line is a half turn, and a half turn is 2 right angles.

sets.title: Horizontal, vertical, parallel and perpendicular lines

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does this rectangle have?
items.e: The top and bottom sides are parallel, and the left and right sides are parallel. That is 2 pairs (4 is the number of sides).

items.q: What are perpendicular lines?
c: lines that meet at a right angle
lines that meet at any angle
items.e: Perpendicular lines meet or cross at a right angle. The corner of a page has two perpendicular edges.

items.q: Ethan says these lines cannot be parallel because they are not horizontal. Is he right?
c: No, parallel lines can go any way
Yes, parallel lines must be horizontal
items.e: These vertical lines stay the same distance apart, so they are parallel. Parallel lines can be horizontal, vertical or slanting.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: Picture A shows lines that stay the same distance apart all the way along, so they will never meet. The lines that get closer would meet if they were longer.

items.q: A horizontal line and a vertical line meet. What are they?
items.e: A horizontal line and a vertical line meet at a right angle, so they are perpendicular.

items.q: Which pair of lines is parallel?
items.e: Picture C shows lines that stay the same distance apart, even though they slant. Parallel lines do not have to be horizontal or vertical.

items.q: Which two sides of this triangle are perpendicular?
items.e: Sides AB and AC meet at corner A, which is a right angle. So AB and AC are perpendicular.

items.q: Which capital letter has lines that are perpendicular?
items.e: The 2 lines of L meet at a right angle. The lines in V, X and N meet at a slant.

items.q: What can you say about the two rails of a railway track?
items.e: The rails stay the same distance apart so the train can run on them. They look like they meet far away, but they never do: they are parallel.

items.q: How many vertical lines are in the capital letter H?
items.e: The 2 sides of H go straight up and down, so they are vertical. The middle line goes across: it is horizontal.

items.q: Which line is vertical?
items.e: Picture B goes straight up and down, like a flagpole. That is a vertical line. The line going straight across is horizontal.

items.q: The line where the sea meets the sky goes straight across. What kind of line is it?
items.e: A line that goes straight across is horizontal. The word comes from horizon, where the sea meets the sky.

items.q: Which line is horizontal?
items.e: Picture D goes straight across, like the horizon. That is a horizontal line. The line going straight up and down is vertical.

items.q: A flagpole stands straight up and down. What kind of line does it make?
items.e: Straight up and down is vertical. Horizontal lines go straight across, like the horizon.

items.q: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.e: Picture B shows lines that meet at a right angle: they make square corners. They are turned, but the angle is still a right angle.

items.q: Which pair of lines is perpendicular?
items.e: Picture D shows lines that meet at a right angle (a square corner). The other crossing lines meet at a slant, not at a right angle.

items.q: How many horizontal lines are in the capital letter E?
items.e: The top, middle and bottom lines of E go straight across: 3 horizontal lines. The line on the left is vertical.

items.q: Which capital letter has a pair of parallel lines?
items.e: The 2 upright lines of H are parallel. L, T and V have no lines going the same way.

items.q: What are parallel lines?
c: lines that meet at a right angle
lines that stay the same distance apart and never meet
lines that cross in the middle
lines that go straight up and down
items.e: Parallel lines always stay the same distance apart, like railway tracks. They never meet, however long they are.

items.q: Lily says these lines are parallel because they do not touch. Is she right?
c: No, they get closer and would meet
Yes, lines that do not touch are parallel
items.e: The gap on the left is bigger than the gap on the right. If the lines were longer, they would meet. Parallel lines stay the same distance apart.

items.q: What angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 1 o’clock the hands are only 1 hour mark apart. That is narrower than a right angle (3 hour marks).

items.q: Aisha makes a quarter turn clockwise, then another quarter turn clockwise. What turn is that altogether?
items.e: 2 quarter turns make a half turn: 2 right angles.

items.q: How many minutes does the minute hand take to make a quarter turn?
items.e: A whole turn of the minute hand takes 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 15, so a quarter turn takes 15 minutes.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from the dashed line to where it is now. What turn has it made?
items.e: From 12 to 3 is a quarter of the way round the clock: a quarter turn.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from the dashed line to where it is now. What turn has it made?
items.e: From 3 to 9 is halfway round the clock: a half turn.

items.q: Zara faces the board. She turns clockwise through 3 right angles. What turn is that?
items.e: Each right angle is a quarter turn. 3 quarter turns make a three-quarter turn.

items.q: Amelia faces west. She makes a three-quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face now?
items.e: Count 3 quarter turns clockwise from west: north, east, south.
The hand goes all the way round from 9 back to 9: a whole turn.

items.q: Oliver opens a door until it makes a square corner with the wall. What turn has the door made?
items.e: A square corner is a right angle, and a right angle is a quarter turn.

items.q: Which road is parallel to High Street?
items.e: Mill Lane goes across the map, the same way as High Street, and they stay the same distance apart. So they are parallel.

items.q: Mohammed walks north. He turns right. Which way is he walking now?
items.e: Turning right is a quarter turn clockwise. A quarter turn clockwise from north is east.

items.q: What angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 hour marks apart. A right angle is only 3 hour marks, so this angle is greater.

items.q: It is 2:00 pm. The minute hand makes a half turn. What time is it now?
items.e: A half turn of the minute hand is 30 minutes. 30 minutes after 2:00 pm is 2:30 pm.
From 6 round to 3 is 6 to 9, 9 to 12 and 12 to 3: 3 quarter turns. That is a three-quarter turn.

items.q: Charlie faces south. He makes a quarter turn anticlockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Anticlockwise goes S, E, N, W. A quarter turn anticlockwise from south is east.

items.q: Which road is perpendicular to High Street?
items.e: Station Road goes up and down the map and meets High Street at a right angle. Park Road crosses at a slant, not at a right angle.

items.q: What angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands make a square corner: a right angle.

items.q: Poppy spins round in the playground until she faces the same way again. What turn has she made?
items.e: Facing the same way again means going all the way round: a whole turn.

items.q: Freya faces east. She makes a half turn. Which way does she face now?
items.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. West is opposite east.

items.q: At which junction do the roads meet at a right angle?
items.e: Picture B has a side road that meets the main road at a square corner. The other roads meet at a slant.
